findings.mechanism: Any persisted non-autonomy decidedBy is classified as a human decision. Approvals made by an authorized bearer API token have a non-autonomy actor label, so automated API decisions are presented as completed human review. A display label alone does not establish a human principal.
findings.evidence: auth/service.ts:434 resolves API tokens with label API token “name”; auth/http.ts:45 actorOf returns that label; app.ts:703-706 passes it to decideProposal, which saves it in decidedBy (visua.ts:1903). An inline execution of agentStages with an applied proposal decidedBy=API token “automation” returned {id:review,state:complete,detail:1 human decision.}.
findings.recommendation: Use neutral recorded-decision wording when the persisted source is only a label, or persist an explicit decision principal kind and distinguish human, API-token, autonomy and unknown sources. Add a regression using the real token actor shape without changing exact approval-token enforcement.

findings.mechanism: For interrupted runs, current is selected from every displayed stage whose state matches the run status. A legacy failed run with a failed proposal therefore acquires current=apply, even though its runtime failure stage is unrecorded. Proposal application failure can have occurred earlier than an unrelated agent execution failure, so the heading invents a runtime boundary.
findings.evidence: Inline source execution with run.status=failed, no stageHistory, run.error=Model connection closed, and one failed autonomous proposal produced collect/analyze=not-recorded, apply=failed, current=apply, summary=Run failed during Apply. The projection inferred the summary from the proposal state rather than a recorded runtime stage.
findings.recommendation: Attribute an interrupted runtime stage only from persisted collect/analyze start/completion facts. Leave legacy runtime stage unknown while retaining the separate failed application outcome. Add the failed legacy run plus failed proposal regression.

findings.mechanism: Tier drafts are retained only while ProfileWorkspace remains mounted. Shell observes the same workspace summary query and returns its error screen on any background summary refetch error, even when cached data exists. After a user edits tier answers, a transient summary refresh failure unmounts ProfileWorkspace; retry mounts fresh state from the saved assessment and silently loses the draft. The local tier error branch cannot retain state through this ancestor unmount.
findings.evidence: ProfilePage.tsx initializes answers from existing?.answers and dirty=false in local state; its dirty guard only operates in that mounted component. Shell.tsx:444-446 subscribes to the route/canonical summary, and line 488 replaces the entire provider/outlet for summary.error. events.ts invalidates the summary after workspace activity, and useWsMutation also invalidates it. This is a deterministic source-traced lifetime issue, not a browser reproduction. Existing e2e tests cover POST-save failure and tab changes but not GET-summary refetch failure.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the mounted workspace subtree and show a refresh error for transient failures when its same-identity cached data remains usable, or retain drafts above that error boundary keyed by workspace identity. Continue to handle actual access loss appropriately. Verify editing tier answers, forcing a summary refresh 503, retrying, and retaining those answers.

limitations: No application edits, browser/server/build runs, full test suite, PostgreSQL-specific lane or production access were performed. The lead owns integration and browser verification.
The tier draft loss is supported by the actual component/query lifetime trace but was not executed in a browser under the review contract.

Focused unit passes do not cover the two newly reproduced projection edge cases; their current results are the reported failures. This report remains bound to the original snapshot; subsequent lead fixes require their own affected verification.
